patch_description: Replace the random-point initialization with a deterministic optimization. Key geometric facts: (1) random points almost surely create near-collinear triples, giving min triangle area near 0 — hence the current score of 0.01; (2) good Heilbronn configurations place most points near the convex boundary with a few interior points. Strategy: initialize with 12 points on a circle plus the center (a strong symmetric starting configuration), then run a deterministic coordinate-descent refinement: for each point, try moving it in 8 compass directions at several step sizes, keeping any move that increases min-triangle-area / hull-area (the scale-invariant objective). Steps shrink geometrically. All operations are deterministic (fixed seed, structured perturbations), vectorized over all 286 triangles, and fast (< 1s). This reliably pushes the normalized minimum triangle area well above the random baseline and toward the ~0.031 benchmark.
